lines.text: Which hand aged? In four and a half years, one showed no detectable ageing.
lines.phonemes: wˌɪtʃ hˈand ˈeɪdʒd? ɪn fˈɔː and ɐ hˈɑːf jˈiəz, wˈɒn ʃˈəʊd nˈəʊ dɪtˈɛktəbəl ˈeɪdʒɪŋ.

lines.text: They belong to two neighbours in Nambour, a Queensland town where pure chance decided who would wear sunscreen every morning. Head, neck, arms and hands, before the day began.
lines.phonemes: ðeɪ bɪlˈɒŋ tə tˈuː nˈeɪbəz ˈɪn nˈæmbɔː , ˈeɪ kwˈiːnzlənd tˈaʊn wˌeə pjˈʊə tʃˈans dɪsˈaɪdɪd hˌuː wʊd wˈeə sˈʌnskɹiːn ˈɛvɹɪ mˈɔːnɪŋ. hˈɛd, nˈɛk, ˈɑːmz and hˈandz, bɪfˌɔː ðə dˈeɪ bɪɡˈan.

lines.text: It was never sunscreen against none: the others could use it whenever they pleased, or not at all. Researchers read the fine lines in silicone casts of hands.
lines.phonemes: ɪt wɒz nˈɛvə sˈʌnskɹiːn ɐɡˈɛnst nˈɒn: ðɪ ˈʌðəz kʊd jˈuːz ɪt wɛnˌɛvə ðeɪ plˈiːzd, ɔː nˌɒt at ˈɔːl. ɹɪsˈɜːtʃəz ɹˈiːd ðə fˈaɪn lˈaɪnz ɪn sˈɪlɪkˌəʊn kˈasts ɒv hˈandz.

lines.text: It's easy to think sun damage is the burn you feel. But an ultraviolet camera reveals damage the naked eye misses, long before it shows on the surface.
lines.phonemes: ɪts ˈiːzi tə θˈɪŋk sˈʌn dˈamɪdʒ ɪz ðə bˈɜːn juː fˈiːl. bˌʌt ɐn ˌʊltɹɐvˈaɪəlɪt kˈamɹə ɹɪvˈiːlz dˈamɪdʒ ðə nˈeɪkɪd ˈaɪ mˈɪsɪz, lˈɒŋ bɪfˌɔːɹ ɪt ʃˈəʊz ɒnðə sˈɜːfɪs.

lines.text: And they were followed for ten more years. Melanoma, the most serious skin cancer, came out at about half, in numbers too small to be sure.
lines.phonemes: and ðeɪ wɜː fˈɒləʊd fɔː tˈɛn mˈɔː jˈiəz. mˌɛlənˈəʊmə , ðə mˈəʊst sˈiəɹiəs skˈɪn kˈansə, kˈeɪm ˈaʊt at ɐbˌaʊt hˈɑːf, ɪn nˈʌmbəz tˈuː smˈɔːl təbi ʃˈʊə.

lines.text: At a lab's test dose, that morning layer is about a fifth of a paper's thickness.
lines.phonemes: atə lˈabz tˈɛst dˈəʊs, ðat mˈɔːnɪŋ lˈeɪəɹ ɪz ɐbˌaʊt ɐ fˈɪfθ əvə pˈeɪpəz θˈɪknəs.

lines.text: So, which hand aged? Both groups missed mornings; one missed fewer, and the skin kept count.
lines.phonemes: sˈəʊ, wˌɪtʃ hˈand ˈeɪdʒd? bˈəʊθ ɡɹˈuːps mˈɪst mˈɔːnɪŋz; wˈɒn mˈɪst fjˈuːə, and ðə skˈɪn kˈɛpt kˈaʊnt.

lines.text: Next: tanning beds share a list with cigarettes. Same list, same risk?
